channel.title: Progress Software Corporation — recent CVEs
channel.description: Most recent CVEs assigned by Progress Software Corporation (progresssoftware).

item.title: CVE-2026-115340 · 7.1 HIGH — Insecure Storage of Web Transfer Credentials in Progress WS_FTP Server
item.description: Progress Software WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 on Windows may write sensitive user credential and session data to a temporary file during file transfer operations.

item.title: CVE-2026-115339 · 7.5 HIGH 🌩️ — Unauthenticated XFT Memory Exhaustion in Progress WS_FTP Server
item.description: Insufficient resource limits in Progress Software WS_FTP Server releases prior to 2025.0.5 on Windows could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause denial of service.

item.title: CVE-2026-115341 · 7.7 HIGH — Unauthorized File Disclosure via Path Traversal in Thin Client Web Transfer in Progress WS_FTP Server
item.description: Improper access restrictions in the Thin Client Web Transfer component of Progress Software WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 on Windows could allow an authenticated FTP user to access files outside their intended scope.

item.title: CVE-2026-115337 · 6.3 MEDIUM — Folder Permission Bypass in Progress WS_FTP Server
item.description: Improper access control in Progress WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 could allow an authenticated user with certain folder-management permissions to bypass access restrictions and access or modify files belonging to other users.

item.title: CVE-2026-115336 · 6.5 MEDIUM — FTP Quota Accounting Bypass in Progress WS_FTP Server
item.description: Incorrect quota accounting in Progress Software WS_FTP Server releases prior to 2025.0.5 on Windows could allow an authenticated user with upload and delete permissions to exceed storage quotas, potentially causing denial of service.

item.title: CVE-2026-115338 · 8.1 HIGH 🌩️ — Insecure XFT Transport in Progress WS_FTP Server
item.description: Insufficient protection of communications in Progress WS_FTP Server versions prior to 2025.0.5 could allow a network attacker to intercept sensitive information or modify requests when unencrypted connections are used.
